summary.text: A 44-year-old woman with granulomatosis with polyangeitis as baseline disease had been on peritoneal dialysis for 2 years and 11 months, with residual diuresis of 600 mL and an antibody reactivity panel of 0. She received a kidney from a 37-year-old female donor in severe acute kidney injury (initial creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, final 7.4 mg/dL, KDPI 46%, uptake biopsy with signs of ATN).

Cold ischemia lasted 23 hours 30 minutes; induction used methylprednisolone and thymoglobulin with tacrolimus, everolimus and prednisone maintenance. The transplantation occurred without problems and without urologic or vascular complications.

She had delayed graft function with progressive improvement from the second week, was discharged on the 30th postoperative day, and at two years and eight months had creatinine 1.0 mg/dL and GFR 67 mL/min/1.73 m².

summary.text: A 52-year-old patient with unknown baseline disease had been on hemodialysis for 4 years and 11 months, with residual diuresis of 500 mL and an antibody reactivity panel of 34%. The donor was a 43-year-old smoker in severe acute kidney injury (initial creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, final 12.2 mg/dL, KDPI 54%, uptake biopsy ATN).

Induction used methylprednisolone and thymoglobulin 4.5 mg/kg, with tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisone therapy; surgery occurred without complications. Delayed graft function was prolonged, with a biopsy in the 13th postoperative day histopathologically compatible with ATN, urine output increase from the 21st day of hospitalization, several infectious intercurrences (UTI, esophageal moniliasis, cytomegalovirus infection), discharge in the 46th postoperative day, and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL with GFR 98 mL/min/1.73 m² at 5 months 13 days.

article_limitations: Four recipients (Cases 1-4); donors are subject "other" inside the recipient record, and Cases 1 and 2 share one donor (three donors in total).
Table 1 Cr (1)-(7) columns do not state whose creatinine they report, the unit, or the week anchor; their values are kept review_only with subject unknown and no unit added.
Table 1 UO(mL) is undefined (note truncated at "UO:") and not labelled donor or recipient; kept review_only with subject unknown, not merged with the text donor diuresis.
Donor CPK is printed UI/mL in Table 1 but U/L or IU/L in the text (1000-fold unit difference); both sides are review_only source conflicts.
Case 3 is introduced as "Female" but later referred to as "He"; documented sex is a review_only source conflict.

Discussion attributes a long dialysis time to "the first case" and a 25-hour CID to "the third case", which do not match Results (Case 2 has 9 years 5 months and 25 hours 5 minutes); not assigned to any patient. TIF is undefined and not equated to CID.
Case 4 "unknown baseline disease for 1 year and 5 months" is ambiguous in what the duration refers to.
Table 1 Cr (7) values (1.1, 1.6, 0.8, 2.2) are 7th-column values and are different time points from the text "currently" creatinine values; not merged.
No figures, supplements or videos in the source; no visual task is applicable.
